articleTitle: An Examination of Heavy Ion-Induced Persistent Visual Error Signatures in an Electronic Display Driver Integrated Circuit
publicationTitle: 2023 23rd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: Heavy ion irradiation of a display driver integrated circuit (DDIC) was performed, and persistent visual error signatures were captured. Based on the heavy ion results, error signatures were localized to configuration registers motivate potential mitigation techniques and observations relating to single event effect susceptibility. DDICs serve as an integral component of integrated display systems that will require the development of single event effects test methodologies in anticipation of extensive use in crewed spacecrafts outside of the Earth’s geomagnetic protection.

articleTitle: Muon-Induced SEU Cross Sections of 12-nm FinFET and 28-nm Planar SRAMs
publicationTitle: 2023 23rd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: While muon irradiation experiments have been reported in recent years, negative muon irradiation to FinFETs has not been reported. Negative muons have the unique physical property of muon capture reaction, and generated secondary ions have larger linear energy transfer (LET) than muons themselves. We performed positive and negative muon irradiation experiments on 12-nm FinFET and 28-nm planar SRAMs at MUSE in J-PARC. The negative muon-induced single event upset (SEU) cross section is more than ten times larger than that of the positive muon. The negative muon-induced SEU cross section of FinFETs decreases by the same ratio as neutron-induced one compared to planar SRAMs.

articleTitle: Soft Errors Rate Assessment in SRAM and Sequential Circuits manufactured in ST 40 nm BCD Technology
publicationTitle: 2023 23rd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: We investigate radiation robustness of the brand-new high density 40 nm ST BCD MOS technology against soft errors by analyzing both SRAMs and Flip-Flops response after exposure to both alpha particles and heavy ions.

articleTitle: Radiation Effects in Real-Time Soft Processors: Relating Software Errors to Hardware Faults
publicationTitle: 2023 23rd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: In this paper, we propose an analysis of the effects on soft processors of radiation-induced microarchitectural faults propagating to the software level, such as silent data corruption and system exception mechanisms.

articleTitle: Single Event Transient Filtering Transfer Gate: A Layout-Aware Simulation Study
publicationTitle: 2023 23rd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: This paper proposes the single event transient filtering transfer gate (SIFT). A layout-aware simulation of the technology computer-aided design (TCAD) was performed to evaluate the capability of the proposed circuit. The simulation result indicates that the proposed circuit would have a threshold linear energy transfer (LET) between 10 to 40 MeV•cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>/mg, much higher than a normal inverter.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Back End Of Line Rerouting on Single Event Latchup Occurrence in Readout Integrated Circuits
publicationTitle: 2023 23rd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: In this paper, the impact of the rerouting of the back end of line (BEOL) on the occurrence of single event latchup (SEL) in a readout integrated circuit (ROIC) of cooled infrared detectors is presented and discussed. Heavy ions tests have been performed for different temperatures. The change in the BEOL design is investigated by simulation tools. Experimental data and simulation demonstrate that rerouting of the BEOL does not impact the SEL sensitivity of the CMOS device.

articleTitle: Hardening a Neural Network on FPGA through Selective Triplication and Training Optimization
publicationTitle: 2023 23rd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: The proposed approach identifies SEU sensitive flip-flops and optimizes the training phase of a neural network. With this information, selective triplication is applied to improve the reliability with limited resource overhead on an FPGA device.

articleTitle: A Radiation-tolerant, Temperature-Insensitive and Bandwidth-adaptive CPPLL with Synchronous-bias-voltage Technique for SerDes
publicationTitle: 2023 23rd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: This paper presents a synchronous-bias-voltage technique to improve CPPLL's stability and radiation-hardened property. Test results show bandwidth changes about -2.99%-2.41%; jitter’s temperature-drift is 12.1% in -55°C-125°C; unlocked and unrecoverable cross-section decreases from 2*10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-7</sup>cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> to 1*10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-7</sup>cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>.

articleTitle: Low Energy, High Flux, Uniform and Large Field Size Electron Beam Facility
publicationTitle: 2023 23rd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: Materials to be deployed in space applications have to undergo a variety of different test scenarios, simulating actual space conditions. Among these materials solar photovoltaic cells, optics, meta-materials and more will be directly exposed to space radiation and must be tested accordingly. From the design phase of such target materials to the final production, it is important to obtain information about their behavior and performance in defined irradiation scenarios and qualify them following the directions of relevant ECSS/ESA standards [8]. An excellent method to cover part of these tests in a laboratory scale is the high-flux, high-fluence electron irradiation with the help of industrial electron beam generators.The present collaboration has developed different irradiation test setups and procedures, adapted to the existing electron beam generators at IPF in Dresden, Germany covering an energy range between 100 keV to 1.5 MeV. The test setups, aiming for high electron flux, uniform and large irradiation field sizes, and their capabilities for use in irradiation qualification tests for space applications are described in this paper.

articleTitle: Nonlinear Absorption in SiC Photodiode by Ultrafast Laser Irradiation in The Infrared
publicationTitle: 2023 23rd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: Silicon carbide, SiC, is a wide bandgap semiconductor. Though its applications are more confined in comparison with the traditional silicon semiconductor, it can be found in high performance power electronics and demand is growing due to the rising popularity of electric vehicles and the rapid development of commercial satellites. To investigate space radiation effects in SiC devices, typically heavy-ion beams are applied. However, instead of the conventional accelerator-based device testing, a picosecond/femtosecond pulsed laser can be used as an alternative high energy source to facilitate similar radiation effects based on the optical absorption in the semiconductor material. Besides evaluating the device susceptibility to the radiation damage, additional information such as 2D/3D spatial mapping of the sensitive regions in the circuitry can be extracted from focused laser testing. For preliminary laser-based testing, a commercial SiC photodiode was used as the sample device to study its optical absorption characteristics in the infrared spectral regime. From the experiments, electron-hole pair generation was found to involve the absorption of multiple photons and, possibly, multiple phonons. Thus, the feasibility of using an ultrafast infrared laser as the high energy source in simulating the radiation effects in wide bandgap SiC devices is not unattainable.

articleTitle: Radiation-Enhanced Multi-Level Cell Behavior in TaOx/NiO-based Resistive Random Access Memory
publicationTitle: 2023 23rd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: As a non-volatile memory (NVM), resistive random-access memory (RRAM) has been considered as one of the promising emerging devices to emulate the synaptic behavior and accelerate the computation of intelligent algorithms. In addition, compared to conventional NVMs, RRAM has the advantage of higher radiation tolerance and application prospects in space. In this work, the radiation effects on bilayer dielectric TaO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>/NiO-based RRAM using <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">60</sup>Co γ-ray were investigated. Devices were irradiated up to a dose of 400 krad (Si) and exhibited changes in characteristics which might be caused by the increase of oxygen vacancies within the dielectric layers as a result of irradiation. The irradiated device also displayed an enhanced multi-level cell (MLC) behavior controllable under lower compliance currents, compared to pristine devices.

articleTitle: Heavy-ion and proton Single Event Effect (SEE) characterization of 7nm FinFET AMD VersalTM
publicationTitle: 2023 23rd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: This paper presents the test setup and SEE results recently obtained under heavy ions and protons on 7nm FinFET Xilinx Versal™, the latest product proposed by Xilinx. Single Event Upset (SEU) Sensitivity curves are presented for both memories from processing system (PS) and programmable logic (PL) units. Single Event Functionnal Interrupt (SEFI) are also discussed. Occurrence rate have been also calculated at different representative orbits.

articleTitle: Neutron-Induced Error Rate of Vision Transformer Models on GPUs
publicationTitle: 2023 23rd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: Vision Transformers (ViTs) are the new trend to improve performance and accuracy of machine learning. Through neutron beam experiments we show that ViTs have a higher FIT rate than traditional models but similar error criticality.

articleTitle: Proton and Neutron SEB Testing and Electrical Analysis on 4H-SiC MOSFETs and Diodes
publicationTitle: 2023 23rd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: In this study, we tested and analyzed SiC power MOSFET and SiC diode in both standard neutron and proton accelerator facilities. Base on the test, we found degradation of transfer characteristics and transconductance in SiC power devices under neutron and proton beam. Single event effects (SEE) tolerance and correlation between the both beams test results are also analyzed.

articleTitle: Neutron- and Proton-Induced Degradation of MOS Transistors in 28 nm CMOS Technology (September 2023)
publicationTitle: 2023 23rd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: The 28 nm CMOS technology was selected as a promising candidate for upgrade of the electronics of particle detectors at CERN. Despite the robustness of this node to ultrahigh levels of total ionizing dose has been proven, the capability to withstand 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">16</sup> 1 MeV neq/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> fluences is still unknown. Displacement damage effects on two 28 nm CMOS technology processes were therefore investigated through proton and neutron irradiation up to the fluences of interest for high energy physics applications. N-type and p-type core and I/O transistors with different sizes were studied. The results of the extensive irradiation campaign revealed that the 28 nm CMOS node was indeed affected by either proton or neutron. However, through X-ray irradiation was possible to determine that the observed radiation-induced degradation was caused by the amount of total ionizing dose deposited during neutron and proton exposure rather than displacement damage. These results prove that 28 nm CMOS technology is suitable for applications in CERN’s particle detectors.

articleTitle: Assessment of SER Predictions for Radiation Hardness Assurance of SRAMs in Harsh Proton Space Environments
publicationTitle: 2023 23rd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: In this paper, prediction methodologies to compute SER are discussed due to the limitations of relevant parameters of current methods for sub nanometer devices under heavy ions but mostly protons. Attention is focused on the direct ionization of low energy protons, the SEU cross section dependance on the incident protons angle and the modelling of the spacecraft geometry.

articleTitle: Radiation Responses of Pure-Silica Core Multimode Optical Fibers in the UV to near-IR Domains at MGy Dose Levels
publicationTitle: 2023 23rd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: We study the Radiation-Induced Attenuation (RIA) of four solarization-resistant commercially-available optical fibers manufactured by Polymicro, optimized for the transmission ranging from the Deep Ultra-Violet (DUV) to the Near InfraRed (NIR). The different contents of hydroxyl groups (Si-OH) play a key role on their RIA levels and kinetics, revealing the predominant contribution of Non-Bridging Oxygen Hole Centers absorption bands in high-OH samples. In the low-OH sample and in another sample with unspecified OH content (dedicated to a broad-spectrum transmission), Cl-related species are the most impacting on the RIA in our investigated spectrum range. The application potential of these fibers at MGy dose levels is here discussed.

articleTitle: L2-Charged Particle Environment (L2-CPE) Low Energy Radiation Fluence Model
publicationTitle: 2023 23rd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: The L2-CPE engineering model specifies low energy electron, proton, and alpha particle environments in the solar wind and Earth’s distant magnetosheath and magnetotail at energies of importance to surface dose in space exposed materials.

articleTitle: Neutron damage analysis in single- and dual-layer 150 nm CMOS SPADs
publicationTitle: 2023 23rd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: The study presented in this paper focuses on the effects of neutrons on the dark count rate (DCR) performance of single photon avalanche diodes (SPADs) fabricated in a 150 nm CMOS technology. Three chips, one of which consisting of a dual-layer structure, with two dice face-to-face bump bonded, were exposed to increasing fluences of neutrons, up to around 4.3×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</sup> 1 MeV neutron equivalent cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−2</sup>, from a non-monochromatic source, with energies ranging from a few hundreds of keV to a few MeV. In the analysis of radiation damage, attention was paid in particular to two of the four SPAD arrays embedded in the chips, one including 2304, the other 1728 cells, featuring different sensitive area. Characterization results prove that, for a given fluence, bi-layered SPADs can preserve much lower DCR levels than single-layer ones.

articleTitle: Analyzing the SEU-induced Error Propagation in Systolic Array on SRAM-based FPGA
publicationTitle: 2023 23rd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: In this paper, we evaluated the radiation-induced Single Event Upset of an open-source TPU-like platform implemented on SRAM-based FPGA while its high-performance parallel datapath is exploited to implement multiple feature extractions task.

articleTitle: Defects studies towards more-radiation-tolerant Silicon Photomultipliers
publicationTitle: 2023 23rd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: Silicon photomultipliers (SiPMs) are single-photon sensitive large-area detectors widely used in many applications. Among them, they are used in several radiation-harsh applications, like high-energy physics and experiments in space, where they receive a significant radiation dose. The effect of ionizing and non-ionizing radiation dose on their performance is very interesting for those applications.We irradiated several Silicon Photomultipliers with protons and X-ray. We investigated the noise increment and directly compared per performance worsening on several SiPM technologies produced sat FBK (Trento, Italy). We also characterized the temperature dependence of the noise down to cryogenic levels, extracting the activation energy. We investigated in depth the defects created by protons within the microcells of the SiPMs, with emission microscopy measurements. We also investigated the effect of ionizing-energy-loss in the SiPM microcells, showing a relevant effect of charge accumulation in the dielectrics and in the trenches. Some technologies demonstrated a worse radiation tolerance with an internal modification of electric fields that increases the primary noise and afterpulsing. This have been directly confirmed with a dedicated irradiation campaign comparing SiPMs with different materials inside the deep trenches between microcells.All these considerations are useful to develop new SiPM technologies that are more radiation hard, both in terms of bulk damage and ionizing-energy-loss effects.

articleTitle: Long-term On-Orbit Upset Rate Prediction of 28-nm UTBB FD-SOI Technology
publicationTitle: 2023 23rd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: This work predicts the long-term on-orbit upset rate of 28-nm ultra-thin body and buried oxide (UTBB) fully depleted silicon on insulator (FD-SOI) technology. This prediction is based on investigating the effect of aging degradation mechanism on the heavy-ion single event upset (SEU) radiation sensitivity of 28-nm UTBB FD-SOI technology utilizing a custom designed test vehicle: ProArray. A comprehensive framework is presented to investigate the underlying mechanisms of the impact of the NBTI degradation mechanism on the heavy-ion radiation susceptibility. The framework can be used to predict the long-term on-orbit upset rate of 28-nm UTBB FD-SOI technology if there is no available experimental data.

articleTitle: Exploring the Effect of Back-Gate Bias on Stability of DSOI SRAM-Based Physical Unclonable Function
publicationTitle: 2023 23rd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: Two types of SRAM PUF were tested under various back-gate bias. The bit error rate can be reduced by 4.1% and 11.46% through selecting appropriate transistor type and back-gate bias before and after radiation.

articleTitle: Correlation of High Energy Proton and Atmospheric Neutron Destructive and Non-Destructive Single-Event Effect Tests of a 1200V SiC MOSFET
publicationTitle: 2023 23rd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: We present the correlation of high energy proton and atmospheric neutron single-event test results on a recent 1200V SiC MOSFET, obtained with destructive and non-destructive methods. The correlation of the results is discussed, showing a good agreement between both methods. TCAD modelling is used to investigate the failure mechanisms.

articleTitle: Long-Term Measurements of Solar Particle Events and Inner Belt Protons by GOSAT
publicationTitle: 2023 23rd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: The Light Particle Telescope (LPT) onboard the Greenhouse gases observing satellite (GOSAT, 2009 to present) measured almost the entire 24-cycle period of solar activity (December 2008 to February 2019) with the same sensor, acquiring trapped protons (400 keV to 37 MeV) and the impact on low Earth orbit (LEO) of all solar energetic protons generated during the 24 cycle period.The 4 MeV protons affect solar paddle degradation, and the impact of solar high-energy particles and trapped protons on LEO satellites may be comparable or several times different, depending on the activity of each solar cycle. We observed clear variations that correlate inversely with the solar radio wave strength (F10.7), as well as a clear range of variation in flux per energy. These observations provide important data for the design and operation of low Earth orbit spacecraft and instruments.

articleTitle: Effects of X-ray and Cobalt 60 irradiations on advanced Si/SiGe:C HBTs DC characteristics
publicationTitle: 2023 23rd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: The impact of X-ray and cobalt 60 irradiations on the DC characteristics of two advanced BiCMOS technologies, Si/SiGe:C HBTs, is compared and analyzed. The effects of geometry, post-irradiation time, and annealing are investigated.

articleTitle: The Influence of Bias, LET and Fluence on Latent Damage Induced by Heavy Ions in SiC MOSFETs
publicationTitle: 2023 23rd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: The influence of bias, incident ion linear energy transfer (LET) and fluence on latent damage induced by heavy ions in SiC MOSFETs was experimentally studied. 1200V SiC MOSFETs from four manufactures were tested. Experimental results indicated that the generation of latent damage in these MOSFETs was a positive function of bias, incident ion LET, and fluence. As bias, LET and fluence increased, more latent damage was generated. Single event gate rupture (SEGR) occurred due to latent damage during post irradiation gate stress (PIGS) testing. The stress time needed to trigger SEGR may exceed one second. It was concluded that the bias, LET and fluence used to evaluate SiC MOSFET degradation due to latent damage should be calculated based on spacecraft orbit and mission period. Further research on PIGS time is necessary.

articleTitle: Embedded Total Ionizing Dose Estimator exposed to large ionizing doses via focused and pulsed X-ray beam
publicationTitle: 2023 23rd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: This paper presents the response of an embedded Total Ionizing Dose Estimator exposed to large ionizing doses produced by the ID09 time-resolved synchrotron X-ray beamline at ESRF. Results are compared to a <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">60</sup>Co gamma irradiation.

articleTitle: TID System-Level Testing and Qualification Methodology of COTS SD and SSD NAND Flash Memories
publicationTitle: 2023 23rd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: In this work, we propose a system-level test methodology to qualify a set of SD and SSD COTS SLC, MLC and TLC and 3D NAND Flash memories exposed to ionizing radiation. The radiation of the devices under high energy X-rays cause electrical and functional failures of different types. We demonstrate a direct correlation between an increase in current consumption and functional failures in the write speed of each memory. In addition, we show a comparative analysis between 2D and 3D NAND FLASH memories in order to select the most appropriate technology for a nuclear decommissioning mission.

articleTitle: Investigation of SEE laser testing for COTS batch screening
publicationTitle: 2023 23rd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: In this work, we evaluate the pulsed laser test method for SEE screening of different procurement lot of COTS devices, w.r.t different nature of SEE. Indeed, in the New Space context, making large use of COTS devices, confirming the sensitivity of a new procured batch through laser test, based on an existing heavy ion data, would help optimizing project cost and schedule. This work then presents both pulsed laser and heavy ion SEE test obtained on several procurement lot of four COTS devices types. Results show the very good agreement between heavy ions and pulsed laser tests data, demonstrating a comparable efficiency of these two characterizations means in tracking relevant traceability changes from SEE perspective.

articleTitle: Review of Alternatives to Heavy Ions Broad Beam for SEL Screening of COTS
publicationTitle: 2023 23rd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: In the New Space context, more and more industrials consider Commercial Off The Shelf (COTS) components in their design for space equipment, i.e. non-hardened products. The need for qualification of those devices, mainly to destructive effects, is thus growing. As a consequence, beam time at heavy ion broad beam facility is becoming increasingly hard to obtain, as well as being expensive. In the meantime, cheaper and effective alternatives to heavy ion broad beam may be valuable for a pre-screening of the sensitivities of devices to destructive events. This study has thus been motivated by the CNES (Centre National d’Etudes Spatiales) for evaluating the alternatives for pre-selecting good COTS candidate for flight missions. Three alternative methods were thus investigated: pulsed X-rays, pulsed laser and Cf252 source. The sensitivity of several devices, known to be sensitive to Single Event Latchup under heavy ions, is evaluated with those alternative facilities.

articleTitle: Worst Case Heavy Ion Testing Conditions for Normally Off GaN-Based High Electron Mobility Transistor
publicationTitle: 2023 23rd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: Single Event Effect of GaN HEMT devices is usually done using the same testing conditions as the one developed and validated a long time ago for MOSFETs components. This paper presents two alternative SEE testing conditions on normally ON power GaN HEMTs to investigate for worst case that are switching condition and a high tilt beam condition. Test bench and sample preparation for the SEE test campaign are presented and discussed. Finally, alternative testing conditions results are compared to classical SEE testing conditions and Safe Operating Area (SOA) obtained is discussed with the help of TCAD modeling.

articleTitle: Proton Radiation Damage in Silicon Photomultipliers for Gamma-Ray Spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2023 23rd European Conference on Radiation and Its Effects on Components and Systems (RADECS)
abstract: On November 16th, 2020, the Vega mission VV17 carrying the TARANIS Satellite suffered a trajectory deviation, resulting in the loss of the mission and the XGRE instrument dedicated to Gamma-Ray spectroscopy. Subsequent efforts led to the development of the Fast Gamma-Ray Spectrometer (FGS) with updated technologies. The FGS incorporates Silicon Photomultipliers (SiPM) detectors, GaGG:Ce scintillators, and a rad-hard ASIC. This paper presents the characterization and radiation tests on three SiPM detectors from different manufacturers for potential FGS integration: Advansid RGB4S-P, Hamamatsu S13360-6050, and Onsemi FJ60035. The study uniquely implements an identical measurement protocol, offering a pioneering dataset crucial for detector validation. Results include SiPM dark current and dark count rate (DCR) increases after proton radiation, impacting gamma-ray spectroscopy parameters. The FGS detection module, composed of GaGG crystal scintillators coupled to SiPMs, is detailed, with instrument requirements specifying a maximum incident flux of 5.10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup> photons/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>/s, a detection area of 1000 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, and an energy resolution of ±15% at 511 keV. Proton radiation tests were conducted at the Light Ion Facility of the Université Catholique de Louvain, simulating a sun-synchronous low Earth orbit. The SiPM devices were tested, and their dark current, dark count rate (DCR), photon detection efficiency (PDE), gain, and excess charge factor with afterpulsing and optical crosstalk probabilities, were measured. The impact of SiPM dark noise on energy threshold and resolution in a gamma-ray spectrometer is analyzed. The results reveal differences in end-of-life SiPM performance, highlighting the necessity of cooling strategies. The Hamamatsu S13360-6050 SiPM demonstrates superior performance, meeting energy threshold, and resolution specifications without requiring temperature reduction. This study contributes valuable insights for the design and selection of SiPMs in spaceborne gamma-ray spectrometry applications.
